questions.prompt: A frequency table lists the number of visitors to a gallery across five consecutive time periods with frequencies $12, 19, 25, 18, 6$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the cumulative frequencies for all five time periods, and explain why the final cumulative frequency must equal the total number of visitors.

questions.prompt: A student represents grouped data on a cumulative frequency graph. For the class interval $30 \le x < 50$ with cumulative frequency $42$, the student plots the point $(40, 42)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Explain why plotting at $x = 40$ is incorrect, and state the correct coordinate to plot.

questions.prompt: The first class interval in a grouped frequency table of test completion times in minutes is $15 \le t < 25$ with frequency $8$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the coordinates of the starting point of the cumulative frequency graph on the horizontal axis, and state the plotting coordinate for the first class interval.

questions.prompt: The number of pages in a sample of books is recorded in discrete integer classes: $1-50$, $51-100$, and $101-200$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the continuous upper class boundaries at which the cumulative frequencies should be plotted for all three classes.

questions.prompt: Two consecutive points on a cumulative frequency curve are $(20, 18)$ and $(35, 47)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the class interval and the ordinary frequency represented by the step between these two points.

questions.prompt: A student sketches a cumulative frequency graph that slopes downwards between two class boundaries.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Explain why a cumulative frequency graph can never have a negative gradient.

questions.prompt:
The continuous variable $x$ has the frequency distribution shown below:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Class interval} & 0 \le x < 10 & 10 \le x < 20 & 20 \le x < 30 & 30 \le x < 50 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 8 & 14 & 22 & 16 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the cumulative frequency for each class interval.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: State all five points needed to draw the cumulative frequency graph, including the starting point.

questions.prompt:
The ages of $50$ participants in a competition are recorded to the nearest year:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Recorded age (years)} & 20-29 & 30-39 & 40-49 & 50-64 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 6 & 15 & 19 & 10 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the continuous lower boundary of the first class and the continuous upper boundaries of all four classes.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the cumulative frequencies and state the complete set of five plotting coordinates for the cumulative frequency graph.

questions.prompt:
A cumulative frequency graph is constructed from the following set of plotted coordinates:
$$(20, 0),\; (30, 14),\; (45, 44),\; (65, 78),\; (90, 90)$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Determine the total number of observations in this dataset, and state the class interval for the first group.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the ordinary frequency and the frequency density for each of the four class intervals: $20 \le x < 30$, $30 \le x < 45$, $45 \le x < 65$, and $65 \le x < 90$.

questions.prompt:
The travel times $t$ (in minutes) for $100$ commuters are summarized in the table below:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Time } (t\text{ min}) & 0 \le t < 15 & 15 \le t < 25 & 25 \le t < 40 & 40 \le t < 60 & 60 \le t < 90 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 12 & 28 & 35 & 18 & 7 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Construct a cumulative frequency table and list all coordinates needed to draw the cumulative frequency graph.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Using linear interpolation between the plotted points, estimate the median travel time and the number of commuters who take more than 50 minutes.

questions.prompt:
A student was given the following grouped data for the lifetimes $x$ (in hours) of $80$ light bulbs:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Lifetime } (x\text{ hours}) & 400 \le x < 600 & 600 \le x < 800 & 800 \le x < 1000 & 1000 \le x < 1400 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 10 & 26 & 32 & 12 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
The student plotted the points $(500, 10)$, $(700, 36)$, $(900, 68)$, $(1200, 80)$, started the graph at $(0, 0)$, and connected the points with a stepped bar outline.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify three distinct errors made by the student in constructing this cumulative frequency graph.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write down the correct coordinates of all five points for this cumulative frequency graph, and state the cumulative frequency corresponding to the lower quartile.

questions.prompt:
The examination marks $M$ of $160$ candidates are recorded as discrete integer scores from $1$ to $100$:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Mark range } (M) & 1-20 & 21-40 & 41-60 & 61-80 & 81-100 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 16 & 36 & 52 & 40 & 16 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State the continuous lower boundary of the first class and the continuous upper boundaries of all five classes.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the cumulative frequencies and state the complete set of six coordinates needed to plot the cumulative frequency graph.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: To pass the examination, a candidate must score in the top $25\%$ of all candidates. Using linear interpolation between the cumulative frequency coordinates, estimate the minimum pass mark to the nearest integer.

questions.prompt:
An incomplete grouped frequency table and cumulative frequency distribution are shown for the masses $w$ (in grams) of $200$ manufactured items:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Mass } (w\text{ g}) & 50 \le w < 70 & 70 \le w < 90 & 90 \le w < 110 & 110 \le w < 140 & 140 \le w < 180 \\ \hline \text{Frequency} & 24 & p & 64 & q & 16 \\ \hline \text{Cumulative frequency} & 24 & 68 & r & 184 & 200 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the missing values $p$, $q$, and $r$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: State the complete set of six plotting coordinates for the cumulative frequency graph, and identify the median class.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Using linear interpolation between the cumulative frequency coordinates, estimate the interquartile range (IQR) of the masses.
